name: PT Mitra Investindo Tbk

frontmatter.title: Mitra Investindo - a logistics and shipping name pivoting to silica
frontmatter.summary: PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI.JK) is an Indonesian logistics and shipping company developing silica sand mining and an industrial estate. Our SELL rating (target Rp83, -64.6% downside) reflects a price that capitalises an unproven silica project at many times our look-through value. It is a valuation call, not a view that the company is failing: the target deliberately carries the overvalued multiple leg.
thesis: The company's pivot to owned-vessel logistics (revenue growth and margin details in segment discussion [S2]) is margin-enhancing but coincides with revenue erosion (recent decline reported [S3]). Low-margin third-party work has exited; growth depends on silica-haulage and KEK tenant absorption, starting the next few years.

Silica-project development is capital (budget noted [S4]) and carries permitting risk (centralisation of licensing authority [S2]). The option is valuable, but the market is pricing a near-certain commercial outcome that we ascribe a low probability.

The balance-sheet window offered by the recent placement (proceeds detailed [S2]) closes quickly: forecast capex is a high percentage of revenue, free cash turns sharply negative, and dividends stay zero for several years.

catalysts.event: Completion of AMDAL and the feasibility study for the upgrade to IUP Operasi Produksi (silica mining)
First silica sand production and commencement of KEK infrastructure (base case)

blocks.text: We initiate coverage on PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI.JK) with a **SELL** rating and a target price of Rp83, implying -64.6% downside from the current Rp234. The call is a valuation gap, not a bearish view of a business in transition: the group is moving from third‑party logistics chartering to owned‑vessel operations and silica‑sand mining, a base case in which margins recover and revenue grows, but from a starting point far below where the shares trade. The target deliberately keeps the multiple leg at its overvalued value, so the gap is, if anything, understated.

**What the market prices.** At Rp234 (a twelve‑month range of Rp137 to Rp444) the market is valuing the silica project as a near‑certainty -- production slated for late 2026, ramping haulage volumes through FY2030, and the KEK industrial estate attracting tenants [S5, S4, S2]. Free float is tight (19.2%) and insider holdings are 82.0% [S2], restricting supply.

**Our view.** The silica timeline will almost certainly slip. The regulatory shift of silica licensing authority from regional to central government introduces uncertainty (the company's own report flags this as a "primary risk" [S2]); the annual report dedicates 2026 to construction and pre-production, with AMDAL and the feasibility study needed before any IUP Operasi Produksi can even be applied for [S2]. Core logistics revenue fell year on year in 9M2026 [S3] as low‑margin third‑party work exited; operating margins have compressed sharply, with our FY2026E EBITDA margin of 5.2% against 14.0% in FY2025A [S3]. Until silica production commercialises -- our bull case, one of the two tail scenarios -- the company's transition will see negative free cash flow and zero dividends.

The SELL recommendation follows the most‑likely‑base‑case discipline: we value what exists (the logistics and shipping franchise plus the silica option at risk‑adjusted sunk cost), not what the company hopes to build. On a trailing EV/EBITDA the shares price a recovery that depends on timely silica execution, a return to earlier margins, and the capacity to fund the guided silica capex without diluting equity. Our scenarios mirror the revenue‑growth and gross‑margin shocks on either side of the base case; the base value falls between the DCF‑FCFF and the EV/EBITDA cross‑check because the primary method captures the negative‑cash‑flow drag better. The revenue‑growth rate implied by today's price is far above our own long‑run assumption.

**Key value moves:** (a) an OP-IUP granted for silica mining, (b) silica-haulage logistics volumes commencing in FY2027, (c) a restoration of the group freight-day utilisation toward pre-2024 levels (PKL fleet utilisation fell after the 2025 restructuring), and (d) any acceleration in KEK tenancy commitments -- a catalyst absent from public disclosure. The reverse-DCF cannot reach the current price on any revenue-growth assumption we can defend; we think that is unrealistic for Indonesia’s domestic logistics market [S2].

PT Mitra Investindo Tbk (MITI.JK) is an Indonesian logistics and shipping group founded in 1993 as a finance company, now listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) since 1998 [S2]. It operates through three business segments: **shipping services** (Rp61.7bn revenue in FY2025A), **ship management and agency** (Rp43.6bn) and **logistics/stevedoring services** (Rp117.1bn, the largest segment) [S2, F30‑F32]. The group is pivoting from being a logistics service broker to an asset‑owner with an entry into silica‑sand mining and an associated Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in West Kalimantan.

**Segments and mix.** The 2025 annual report presents the business as three segments [S2]: - **Shipping** (Pelayanan Pelayaran): chartering of owned and third‑party vessels for bulk and containerised cargo transport, principally serving the mining and commodity sectors. The segment saw gross profit rise more than tenfold year on year in FY2025A on a revenue decline of roughly a quarter -- the result of "focus on chartered owned‑vessels, which yield higher margins compared to non‑owned vessels" [S2]. The company owns four tugboats and small landing‑craft tankers (LCTs) under subsidiary PT Pelayaran Karana Line (PKL) [S2]. - **Ship management and agency** (Pengelolaan dan Keagenan Kapal): provides vessel crewing, technical management and port‑agency services. Revenue fell modestly year on year in FY2025A to Rp43.6bn while gross profit rose by around a fifth "mainly driven by the Company's ability to optimize cost efficiency" [S2]. - **Logistics/stevedoring** (Jasa Logistik): stevedoring (cargo handling) and inland logistics; historically the largest segment but revenue declined by roughly a quarter year on year to Rp117.1bn in FY2025A as "decline in vessel visits and tonnage" weighed on volumes [S2]. The segment operates under subsidiary PT Wasesa Line (established 1955) and PT Nusantara Bina Silika (the silica holding entity) [S2].

**Strategy.** The management declares a shift "from quantity toward quality profitability" [S2]. The two strategic pillars are (a) owning rather than chartering vessels (the Rp25.8bn fixed‑asset spend in 9M2026 [S3] acquired tugboats/LCTs), and (b) developing silica mining (a 2,042-hectare exploration licence in Kendawangan, Ketapang, West Kalimantan) and an industrial estate (KEK) to capture downstream demand from glass manufacturing and construction [S4, S5]. The company states it aims to "integrate silica mines ... with the development of an industrial zone managed by the Joint Venture" [S2].

**Geographic footprint.** The company is headquartered in Jakarta, with branch offices in Balikpapan, Tanjung Redeb, Bontang, Samarinda and Cilegon [S2]. Operational areas centre on Kalimantan (silica licences) and Java‑Sumatra shipping lanes.

**Market position.** In Indonesia's fragmented domestic‑shipping and logistics market, MITI is a challenger rather than a leader: its FY2025A group revenue of IDR222.4bn is a fraction of the listed shipping majors, and the scale of its silica ambitions would still place it among Indonesia's smaller industrial‑estate developers [S2]. This positioning is our assessment on the base of the segment and licence disclosure [S2]. The company lacks pricing power in shipping (rates are set by global freight indices) and stevedoring (highly competitive).

**Group structure and controlling shareholder.** The group comprises five subsidiaries and six associates [S2]. Key subsidiaries are PT Wasesa Line (logistics/stevedoring), PT Pelayaran Karana Line (shipping, almost wholly owned since the December‑2022 acquisition), PT Nusantara Bina Silika (silica holding entity), PT Kendawangan Berkah Kersik (KBK) and PT Danau Buntar Kuarsa (DBK) (silica exploration subsidiaries) [S2]. Controlling shareholder is **PT Inti Bina Utama**; other substantial shareholders are **PT Prime Asia Capital** and **Andreas Tjahjadi** [S2]. The free float is 19.2% of 3,750.5m shares outstanding [S2].

**Industry size and growth.** Indonesia's transport and warehousing sector grew 12.53% YoY in 2025 (BPS data, cited by the company) [S2], far outpacing GDP growth of 5.1% [S2]. This reflects infrastructure spending and national‑logistics‑mobility improvement, but sector growth is uneven: containerised freight grew at mid‑single‑digit rates while bulk shipping (coal, palm‑oil, silica) saw volatile volumes depending on export‑licensing and ESG pressures. The silica‑sand market is growing globally (IEA Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 flagged "a surge in demand for silica sand as a primary raw material for solar panels and semiconductor technology" [S2]) but Indonesia's domestic production remains fragmented, with most sand mined near Cipatujah (West Java) and Rembang (Central Java).

**Drivers in our sector deck.** The LOGISTICS_TRANSPORT desk models revenue growth tied to GDP (nominal growth in the high single digits in the macro‑deck) and unit costs indexed to inflation (3.28%). For MITI, the specific drivers are: - **Silica demand:** Glass manufacturing (construction) and solar‑panel production. The company cites Freeport as a potential offtaker for silica‑derived construction materials [S2]. - **Shipping‑rate recovery:** Container‑shipping rates stabilised in 2025 after a post‑pandemic collapse; bulk‑shipping rates remain soft. - **Domestic logistics mobility:** BPS's 12.53% sector growth [S2] implies rising vessel‑movement volumes in Kalimantan‑Java corridors.

**Regulation.** Two regulatory risks dominate: (a) centralisation of silica‑sand mining permits from regional governments to Jakarta ("uncertainty regarding the transition ... from Regional Governments to the Central Government" [S2]); and (b) final income‑tax rates for domestic shipping (MITI's shipping subsidiary enjoys a favourable final tax on gross revenue [S3]).

**Competitive landscape.** In shipping, MITI competes with larger listed peers such as PT Samudera Indonesia (SMDR.JK) and PT Temas (TMAS.JK), plus a swarm of private operators; in logistics/stevedoring, it faces PT Pelayaran Nelly Chandra, PT Pelayaran Tanker Timur, and terminal operators like PT Jakarta International Container Terminal. MITI's scale is modest -- FY2025A group revenue was IDR222.4bn [S2], a fraction of the listed shipping majors; the peer comparison is our assessment rather than a company disclosure.

**Moat assessment.** The company's moat is shallow [S2]: - **Cost advantage:** None -- vessels are either owned (PKL's fleet) or chartered at spot rates; crew costs follow unionised wages. Silica mining has no demonstrable grade or cost advantage. - **Network effects:** Its logistics footprint across Balikpapan, Tanjung Redeb, Bontang gives some customer‑lock‑in, but competitors operate similar networks. - **Switching costs:** Low: shipping contracts are typically annual at most; stevedoring contracts are tender‑based. - **Intangible assets:** Brand recognition is minimal outside its niche; the "Mitra Investindo" name is not a premium brand in logistics.

**Five‑forces view** (Porter's framework applied, on the segment disclosure [S2]): - **Rivalry:** High -- dozens of shipping/logistics players compete on price. - **Threat of substitutes:** Moderate -- for some cargo, trucking or rail can replace coastal shipping; silica sand can be sourced from other regions. - **Buyer power:** High -- shipping customers (mining and agri‑commodity companies) command volume discounts and can switch providers. - **Supplier power:** High -- vessel‑crew wages are union‑set; fuel prices are global‑indexed. - **Barriers to entry:** Low for trucking/logistics; moderate for shipping (capex for vessels).

**External influences.** The key macro influences are: (a) **USD/IDR** (house deck 18,350 for FY2027E, a touch above spot) -- shipping invoices are often in USD, benefitting from IDR depreciation; (b) **coal‑export policy** -- Kalimantan's mining activity drives shipping/logistics demand, as the company's risk section sets out [S2]; (c) **silica‑licensing centralisation** -- a regulatory risk flagged by management [S2]; (d) **fuel surcharges** -- bunker‑fuel volatility (tracked in the deck's oil section).

**Revenue build and margins.** Group revenue was IDR222.4bn in FY2025A, -24.1% year on year [S2], and is forecast at IDR199.9bn in FY2026E, -10.1% year on year, following the further 9M2026 decline [S3]. The drop is structural: the company intentionally exited low‑margin third‑party chartering, shrinking the shipping segment by roughly a quarter [S2]. Forecast growth resumes in FY2027 and FY2028 (5.0% and 7.0%) on silica‑haulage volumes and new tugboat/LCT capacity (the Rp25.8bn fleet purchase in 9M2026 [S3]). Gross margin improved in FY2025A to 31.7% (vs 22.9% in FY2024A) as the mix shifted to owned‑vessel chartering; but the 9M2026 margin compressed [S3], leading to our FY2026E assumption of 24.9%, rising to 27.5% by FY2030 as the high‑margin silica‑haulage business scales [S3]. EBITDA margin (14.0% in FY2025A) is projected to trough at 5.2% in FY2026E because the largely fixed cost base does not shrink with the exited chartering revenue -- operating expenses rose while revenue fell in 9M2026 [S3] -- not because of D&A, which sits below EBITDA; it recovers to 9.8% by FY2030E.

**Costs.** Direct costs (COGS) are driven by vessel‑crew wages (fixed), fuel (volatile), and port dues; the LK discloses a sharp year‑on‑year reduction in FY2025A to Rp151.9bn on a revenue change of -24.1% [S2] -- evidence of cost‑structure leverage. SG&A/revenue is forecast to stay elevated at 26.0% in FY2026E (versus a lower share in FY2025A) because of salaries and silica‑project corporate overheads, easing to 23.2% by FY2030E as revenue re‑accelerates [S3].

**Cash flow, capex and working capital.** FY2025A operating cash flow was Rp39.1bn; it collapsed to near zero (Rp0.4bn) in 9M2026 [S3]. Capex peaked in 9M2026 at Rp25.8bn of fixed‑asset purchases (tugboats/LCTs) plus Rp4.9bn of silica‑exploration spend [S3]. The company's Rp24.0bn 2026 budget is the fleet programme for tugboat and LCT purchases [S4], which is largely spent within that Rp25.8bn of nine‑month fixed‑asset purchases and is counted once, not added again; a normal Q4 tail then brings FY2026E total capex to IDR39.6bn (19.8% of revenue). Free cash flow turns negative in FY2026 and FY2027 because of this investment cycle. Net working capital rose sharply in 9M2026 [S3] due to customer‑advance build‑up (including Rp17.8bn from Orient Overseas Container Line [F44]), normalising over the horizon.

**Balance sheet health and debt.** The December‑2025 non‑preemptive placement raised Rp59.8bn [S2], lifting cash to Rp209.1bn as of 30 September 2026. Debt is modest: a Rp10.0bn bank loan and a Rp12.2bn third‑party loan at 30 September 2026 [S3]. Net debt/EBITDA is projected to stay negative (net cash) through FY2029E. Goodwill of Rp116.8bn (acquired in the PKL purchase) is a large share of total assets [S3]; exploration‑evaluation assets for silica stand at Rp10.3bn of capitalised cost [S3].

**Capital allocation.** No dividends were declared for FY2024 or FY2025 [S2]; the company's dividend policy states "distribution ... takes into account ... operational performance, cash flow, capital adequacy, and ... Company's financial position to support optimal future growth" [S2]. Our forecast assumes zero payout until FY2029, then a payout of 25.0% of earnings thereafter (DPS of Rp0.6). The placement proceeds are earmarked for fleet and silica capex [S2, S4].

**Earnings‑quality flags.** The three‑year accruals screen (net income less operating cash flow over average total assets) is positive in only one of the last three years and never above one percentage point of assets, against the house ten‑per‑cent red line; the latest year is strongly negative, so earnings have been cash‑backed and the Sloan flag does not fire [S2, S3]. Cash conversion ran at or above net profit in two of the last three years and more than doubled in FY2025A (operating cash flow of Rp39.1bn against net profit of Rp12.4bn) [S2]. The one deterioration is the 9M2026 collapse to Rp0.4bn of operating cash flow [S3], driven by working capital rather than by profit -- net working capital reached 17.0% of forward revenue -- and it is the single most important number to watch. Related‑party revenue is 5.91% of total revenue [F37], moderate. Capitalised exploration spending (silica) of Rp4.9bn in 9M2026 grew against missing commercial‑production visibility [S3]. D&A is understated in the Yahoo data pack, restated from the LK at IDR12.5bn versus a fraction of that in the pack [F10]. The FY2025 consolidated statements carry an unqualified opinion [S2].

**Structure flags**, classified per the house earnings‑quality card. The November‑2025 non‑preemptive placement (proceeds Rp59.8bn, lifting the share count to 3,750.5m) is **optics‑class**: it was struck at an implied price above today's Rp234, before the operating deterioration, and while disclosed and shareholder‑approved it diluted existing holders [S2]. The one‑day trading suspension of 10 September 2025 on a cumulative price and volume rise, with no administrative sanction and no delisting, is **optics‑class** [S2]. Related‑party flows at 5.91% of revenue are disclosed and modest [S2]. No pledged controlling stake is disclosed [S2]. We found no manipulation‑class flag in the sources.

The financial‑analysis method follows the MOST‑LIKELY‑BASE‑CASE card: restate depreciation from the LK so that costs are not calibrated on understated charges; anchor next‑year volume and pricing on the last actual period, with adjustments sourced from company disclosures; let capex follow the company's guided silica budget plus the fleet expenditure already spent; and mirror the company's own dividend suspension and capex funding plan. The model is built on specific facts carried in the fact base: the interim operating loss, the silica capex budget, capitalised silica spend and the fleet spend. The cash build is temporary -- it will be absorbed by silica development over the next two years.

This LOGISTICS_TRANSPORT name is valued using a 75.0%‑weighted DCF‑FCFF (capturing the negative‑cash‑flow trough during fleet/silica investment) and a 25.0%‑weighted EV/EBITDA multiple cross‑check (reflecting the sector's trading multiple). The weighted target is Rp83, rounded to Rp83. WACC-COE build‑up is in *Table

**Primary method: DCF‑FCFF.** The DCF yields Rp58, discounting five explicit‑year cash flows and a terminal value. Terminal growth is the house bookend of 4.0% (Indonesia nominal‑GDP‑plus), consistent with long‑run fade in the industry. The terminal‑value share is high (111.8%) because the explicit‑period cash flows are thin (FY2026E FCFF is negative, at IDR-36.2bn). The DCF's weakness is its sensitivity to small changes in the early forecast years' margin and volume: a small improvement in gross margin adds several rupiah to the value per share.

The DCF‑FCFF template suits a company in capex‑intensive transition: it isolates depreciation (a large share of the P&L), deducts the cash‑tax effect, and properly treats minority‑interest cash leakage. The cash‑flows‑to‑equity method would obscure the minority drain, since a material share of profit stays with non‑controlling owners. The composite weight toward DCF‑FCFF is higher than the peer comparison alone would justify because the company's near‑term free cash flow is negative, and the EV/EBITDA cross‑check is less reliable in that setting.

**Cross‑checks: EV/EBITDA and peer multiples.** The EV/EBITDA multiple method yields Rp115. The engine applies the peer‑median multiple of 8.42× to trailing FY2025A EBITDA (IDR31.0bn), the last actual, which is also the basis on which the peer median is struck -- each peer's trailing reported EBITDA [S0] -- so the multiple and the metric are consistent; net cash is then added, minorities deducted and the bridge items added. It stands 97.8% above the primary DCF, the divergence the engine flags as a warning. The cause is not D&A (EBITDA is struck before D&A): trailing FY2025A EBITDA still contains the high‑margin third‑party chartering work the company has since exited, so the multiple capitalises a revenue base the group will not see again for five years, if ever. The peer set of twelve names includes asset‑light forwarders whose EBITDA converts to cash with far less capex than MITI's fleet and silica‑project outlay [S2, S3]. We therefore keep the multiple as a cross‑check at the house default weight of 25.0% -- no higher, precisely because it is an upper bound struck on EBITDA the group will not repeat -- and do not let it carry the target. A P/E cross‑check is dropped because FY2026E EPS of 0.40 makes the ratio non‑diagnostic. *Table

items: lists the twelve-name set behind that median, including the two named shipping competitors and the high-multiple outliers that pull the median above them.

blocks.text: **Multiple‑survival test.** The DCF terminal value is 111.8% of DCF value, so the SELL is largely a terminal‑value call and must survive a multiple test. The terminal value implies an exit EV/EBITDA of roughly two-fifths of the peer‑median 8.42×, against an entry multiple of about 22.3x on FY2025A and 69.8x on FY2026E. That exit multiple sits below the peer‑median 8.42× and below the multiple at which MITI trades today; it is the arithmetic consequence of a terminal EBIT margin of about 4.3% (below the cost of capital) combined with 4.0% growth. Either the peer multiple is right, in which case the market pays for earnings MITI has not demonstrated, or the terminal margin is too low. The DCF is the floor and the multiple the ceiling; we weight the DCF at 75.0% because the multiple rests on pre‑transition EBITDA. **Is the terminal margin a haircut?** No -- it is a recovery from the last actual. The anchor is the nine months to September 2026: revenue of Rp151.3bn, D&A of Rp9.5bn against a reported operating loss of Rp1.4bn, so EBITDA is thin and the operating margin is still negative [S3, F13, F17, F19]. Our FY2026E reproduces that run-rate, and every terminal assumption sits above it: revenue of IDR254.8bn against the annualised nine-month base, an EBITDA margin of 9.8% against 5.2%, and a gross margin of 27.5% against 24.9% [S2, S3]. The gap to FY2025A (14.0% EBITDA) is explained by what has left the business: logistics and shipping revenue fell by roughly a quarter in FY2025 and again in 9M2026 as low-margin third-party chartering was exited [S2, S3], so FY2025A is not the right anchor for a smaller, higher-mix group. If the recovery is faster than we assume the DCF rises, but the rating does not change: even at FY2025A margins the DCF is a fraction of the price.

**Liquidity.** We apply no liquidity discount. The house screen applies one only below its lowest daily-value bands, and MITI trades IDR4.5bn a day on a 19.2% free float [S3]. The -64.6% downside already assumes an exit at the quoted price; a second illiquidity haircut would double-count the same risk.

**WACC/COE build‑up.** The cost of capital uses the house macro‑deck: risk‑free rate 7.4% (the IDR sovereign ten‑year), mature ERP 4.2%, Indonesia country‑risk premium 2.5%. Unlevered beta is set to the industry average 0.90; with debt at 2.5% of capital at the spot price, levered beta is 0.92. The pre‑tax cost of debt is 9.4% against a 22.0% tax rate, but the debt weight is immaterial. WACC = 11.9%.

**Bridge items and post-balance-sheet review.** Two bridge items are added to the DCF-based value: silica exploration-and-evaluation assets at capitalised cost of Rp10.3bn [S3, F26], and the group's majority share of PT Ketapang Prima Resources, the industrial-estate JV, at its share of the JV's Rp9.7bn of book total assets [S3, F46]. The JV is not yet operating, so we carry it at cost rather than at zero, as the most-likely-base-case card requires; we hold no estimate of its developed value and no tenancy commitment has been disclosed [S2, S4]. Since 30 September 2026, no material events (divestment, dividend, acquisition) have been announced [S2,S3,S4,S5]. The December-2025 placement (Rp59.8bn) is already in the 30 September 2026 cash balance [S2,S3].
**Sensitivity.** *Table

items: shows that value is most sensitive to the terminal-growth assumption and to gross-margin stabilisation. We also tested the margin question the red team raised: restoring the terminal EBIT margin to the FY2025A level (8.3% rather than 4.3%) lifts the DCF value by roughly two-fifths and still leaves it a small fraction of the share price. The SELL does not depend on the terminal-margin assumption; it depends on the price.

blocks.text: **What the price implies.** The reverse-DCF solver cannot bracket Rp234: even at the top of its tested revenue-growth range the model value stays below the price, because working capital and capex scale with revenue and consume the cash. Read the other way, the market capitalisation of IDR877.6bn against a DCF enterprise value of Rp48.1bn means the market is paying more for the silica option than for the entire existing operating business. That is a view about an undisclosed resource, not about disclosed cash flows [S2, S5].
**Downside risks** with assessed likelihood and impact:

items: **Silica‑licencing centralisation stalls IUP‑OP (regulatory) - LIKELIHOOD: Medium, IMPACT: Severe:** The transfer of silica‑sand mining permit authority from regional governments to Jakarta [S2] could delay the IUP‑Operasi‑Produksi beyond 2027, pushing back silica‑haulage revenue by one to two years. The company's own risk‑disclosure identifies this as a "primary risk" [S2]. Knock‑on: the planned KEK industrial‑estate development faces tenant‑absorption delays.

**Silica‑project over‑investment and cost overruns (operational) - LIKELIHOOD: High, IMPACT: Moderate:** The Rp24.0bn FY2026 capex budget [S4] could prove insufficient; additional borrowing would raise net‑debt/EBITDA above zero -- today the company is net‑cash. The model assumes that budget suffices; any shortfall would dilute equity or cut free cash further.

**Logistics competition intensifies, volume/margin squeeze (market) - LIKELIHOOD: High, IMPACT: Moderate:** The exit of low‑margin charter‑brokering has shrunk revenue (the 9M2026 year‑on‑year decline [S3]); competitors could undercut MITI on owned‑vessel rates, delaying the margin recovery to FY2029 and FY2030.

**Fuel‑price spike (macro) - LIKELIHOOD: Medium, IMPACT: Moderate:** Bunker‑fuel price volatility (linked to the deck's oil prices) could elevate the direct‑cost line year on year, compressing gross margin by one or two points.

**USD/IDR depreciation (currency) - LIKELIHOOD: Medium, IMPACT: Mild:** Shipping‑invoiced USD revenue (unquantified) would translate into lower IDR top‑line if IDR appreciates (house deck sees modest appreciation to 18,350 in FY2027E).

**Related‑party concentration (governance) - LIKELIHOOD: Low, IMPACT: Mild:** Related‑party revenue is 5.91% of total [F37]; any shock to those customers would trim revenue but is not a systemic governance breach.

**Liquidity risk (market) - LIKELIHOOD: Low, IMPACT: Severe:** The free float is 19.2% and the three-month average daily value traded is IDR4.5bn, around half a per cent of market capitalisation a day -- enough to trade a normal line, not enough to exit a large position in a stress event [S3]. A market stress-event could widen spreads and restrict exit liquidity.

blocks.text: **Scenario probabilities and values** (*Table

items: **Base case.** The silica timeline holds: AMDAL and the feasibility study are completed on the 2026 schedule and the OP-IUP follows [S2], haulage commences in FY2027 and FY2028, the KEK attracts tenants gradually, and logistics margins rebound to 27.5% by FY2030. Value per share: Rp72 → target Rp81. This is our most likely path.

**Bear case.** Silica permitting slips beyond 2028 on AMDAL/PPKH delays and the centralisation of silica permitting [S2, S5], logistics margins stay at the 9M2026 trough [S3], revenue growth is slower and gross margin lower -- the same two drivers as the bull case, mirrored. The bear also carries the balance-sheet consequence the DCF already embeds: an operating EV of Rp48.1bn against Rp116.8bn of goodwill [F27] leaves a writedown of most of that carrying value, and a second discounted placement funds the capex shortfall. Value Rp62 → target Rp69.

**Bull case.** Silica de-risks: the OP-IUP is granted on the 2026 AMDAL/feasibility timetable and first production starts in FY2027 [S2], the KEK attracts tenants (including the Freeport and construction-glass demand the annual report names [S2]), and the new tugboat/LCT fleet lifts the logistics and shipping mix. The shock is a revenue-growth and gross-margin step, not a project NPV, because the company discloses no resource tonnage, grade, ASP or offtake volume for the 2,042-hectare licence [S5, F39] and we will not invent one; the bridge carries the sunk cost instead. Value Rp90 → target Rp101.

blocks.text: **Why the scenario spread is narrow.** Both tail scenarios shock the same two drivers -- revenue growth and gross margin -- by equal and opposite amounts, so the bear and bull are true mirrors [S2, S3]. The EV/EBITDA leg does not move between scenarios because the engine strikes it on the trailing reported EBITDA, which the forward shocks cannot change; that is a property of the method and another reason it carries the smaller weight. The rating therefore rests on the base case and the gap to the price, not on the tails: even the bull case target of Rp101 sits well below the Rp234 share price.

**Signposts that change our view.** We would upgrade from SELL to HOLD (or eventually BUY) if: - OP-IUP is granted for KBK/DBK licences after the 2026 AMDAL/feasibility work [S2]. - Silica‑haulage contracts are announced (e.g., with Freeport or glass‑manufacturer offtake). - 9M2027 results show logistics‑segment margin above the low twenties on revenue growth above our base case. - The KEK secures its first tenant commitment (material for long‑term revenue‑visibility). Downward trigger: OP‑IUP rejection or indefinite stall of silica permitting; FY2027 revenue growth below our bear case.

**Ownership and control.** Controlling shareholder: **PT Inti Bina Utama**; other substantial shareholders are **PT Prime Asia Capital** and **Andreas Tjahjadi** [S2]. Free float is 19.2%, with 3,750.5m shares outstanding [S2]. The company is not a konglo name (checked via `fund record`). Insider holdings total 82.0%, institution holdings 0.0%.

**Related‑party dealings.** Related‑party revenue in FY2025A was 5.91% of total revenue [F37]. Transactions include vessel‑chartering with PT Bumi Laut Shipping Services and PT Alvi Cipta Sentosa [S2]. Disclosure is adequate but could be deeper: no line‑item break‑up of purchases from related parties is given beyond the aggregate share disclosed [S2].

**Pledged shares.** The annual report does not disclose any pledged shares by the controlling shareholder or directors, and reports no cash or receivables pledged as collateral; the only encumbrance it discloses is a building pledged against the bank loan [S2]. We therefore assume none of the controlling stake is pledged [S2].

**Auditor and opinion.** Auditor: **KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno, Palilingan & Rekan (PKF)**, engagement partner Hansen Bunardi Wijaya, auditor since 2017 [S2 p80]. The opinion on the FY2025 consolidated financial statements, dated 25 March 2026, is unqualified -- "Wajar Dalam Segala Hal yang Material" / fairly stated in all material respects [S2 p35, p93].

**Dividend record.** No dividend declared for FY2024 or FY2025 [S2]. Dividend policy states dividends may be paid after considering "operational performance, cash flow, capital adequacy, and the Company's financial position to support optimal future growth" [S2]. Our forecast sees zero payout through FY2028.

**Board.** The Board of Commissioners comprises Effendi Sugih Wibowo (Independent Commissioner), Muhammad Sam'an (President Commissioner), and Susilo Atma Kj (Commissioner) [S2]. The Board of Directors: Edwinsyah Hanafi (President Director), Rifki Triyanto (Director), and Irwasih (Director) [S2]. Board committees include Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, and Risk Management -- standard for an IDX‑listed company [S2].

**ESG exposures.** This industry faces: - **Environmental:** Ship‑fuel emissions (direct, scope‑one ), ballast‑water treatment, port‑waste discharge. The company's fleet (tugboats/LCTs) is small; emissions are modest relative to listed shipping peers. - **Social:** Labour‑intensive stevedoring, unionised wages, potential port‑safety incidents [S2]. - **Governance:** Related‑party transactions (disclosed), board independence (one independent commissioner of three), dividend‑suspension transparency [S2].

No major ESG controversies are reported in the annual report; the company has not yet published a standalone sustainability report. The risk‑disclosure chapter covers environmental‑compliance ("Ensures operations are conducted in compliance with applicable laws and regulations" [S2]).

**Konglo status.** `fund record show --ticker MITI.JK` returns `konglo: false`. This is not a konglo name; the governance lens defaults to the ownership and control checks above, which rest on the shareholder disclosure in the annual report [S2].
**Dated catalysts** (repeated from the frontmatter):

items: **Late 2026 / early 2027:** AMDAL and feasibility‑study completion for the upgrade to IUP Operasi Produksi (silica mining). The annual report lists completing the AMDAL/FS as the 2026 focus; the OP‑IUP decision follows [S2]. A positive outcome would de‑risk the bull case; a delay or rejection would validate the bear‑case timeline assumptions. Monitor regulatory‑board announcements.

**FY2027:** First silica-sand production and start of KEK infrastructure development in our base case. The January-2025 announcement targeted end-2026 production [S5], but the annual report recasts 2026 as the construction and pre-production year with AMDAL and the feasibility study as the focus before the OP-IUP [S2]; we therefore book haulage revenue from FY2027 and treat an earlier start as bull-case upside.

blocks.text: **KPIs to monitor between updates:**

items: **Volume signal:** Monthly vessel‑utilisation for PKL‑managed tugboats/LCTs (a target of three‑quarters or more, versus an estimated half in 9M2026). Low utilisation would confirm the margin‑pressure narrative.

**Margin signal:** Logistics‑segment gross margin in the quarterly LK filings. Base‑case assumption is 26.2% through FY2027; any quarter‑on‑quarter deterioration below the high teens argues for a darker view.

**Cash‑flow reality:** Quarterly operating cash flow versus net profit. A persistent operating loss (like the 9M2026 shortfall of Rp1.4bn) without a swift recovery would erode the cash balance and capex capacity.
**Capex run‑rate versus guidance:** Actual silica capex spend versus the Rp24.0bn FY2026 budget. Overspend would trigger funding‑gap risk; underspend could signal a project slowdown.
**Silica‑permitting news:** Any announcement confirming or rejecting the OP‑IUP, AMDAL (environmental‑impact assessment) approval, or PPKH (forest‑area release).
**KEK tenant absorption:** No public commitment yet; any LOI or MOU signed for the KEK would support the bull‑case demand story [S2].

blocks.text: **Monitoring frequency:** Quarterly LK filings (IDX requirement) and company press releases (via investor‑relations site). The 9M2026 interim financials [S3] will be refreshed with FY2026 full‑year LK around March‑April 2027.

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for MITI.JK

S4.title: Mitra Investindo (MITI) Genjot Ekspansi Bisnis Silika

S5.title: Mitra Investindo (MITI) Raih IUP Eksplorasi Pasir Silika, Produksi Ditargetkan Tahun Depan

bear.narrative: Logistics margins stay at the 9M2026 level (24.9% group gross margin [S3]) as the low-margin work base does not rebuild, silica permitting slips past 2028 on AMDAL/PPKH delays and the centralisation of silica permitting [S2, S5], and the fleet capex absorbs free cash through FY2028. The bear also carries a goodwill writedown: the DCF EV of the operating business is below the Rp116.8bn goodwill carrying value [F27], and a second discounted placement funds the shortfall.

bull.narrative: The silica project de-risks: the IUP Operasi Produksi is granted on the 2026 AMDAL/feasibility timetable and first production starts in FY2027 [S2], the KEK attracts tenants (including the stated Freeport and construction-glass demand [S2]), and the new tugboat/LCT fleet lifts the logistics and shipping mix; gross margin and revenue grow ahead of plan through FY2028 on a faster ramp, not an earlier start.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -10.1%: 9M2026 revenue is -11.1% yoy [S3] on the exit of low-margin third-party chartering work in logistics; Q4 run-rate adds ~Rp50bn. FY2027E +5%: new tugboat/LCT fleet commissioned (Rp25.8bn fixed-asset spend in 9M2026 [S3]) and silica-haulage logistics starts. FY2028-30E +7/+7/+6%: silica production from FY2027, because the AR frames 2026 as the construction and pre-production year with AMDAL and the feasibility study for the upgrade to IUP Operasi Produksi as the focus [S2], and the earlier end-2026 target in [S5] predates the permitting centralisation; plus KEK tenant absorption. lt 4% = long-run nominal GDP, per house terminal convention.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 24.9%: 9M2026 actual margin (Rp37.75bn on Rp151.31bn) [S3]. FY2027E 26.2%: logistics segment margin at 17.6% in 9M2026 [S3] vs 22.6% a year earlier, with the owned-vessel share of the mix rising and silica haulage adding a new gross-profit pool; a full return to the FY2025 31.7% is not assumed because the margin mix change is structural. FY2028-30E 27-27.5% as owned-asset utilisation improves. lt 27.5%.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 26.0%: 9M2026 opex of Rp39.2bn (+10.3% yoy) [S3] annualised on ~Rp200bn revenue; Rp26.3bn of it is salaries [S3], a largely fixed base. FY2027-30E falls to 24.7-23.2% as revenue re-accelerates onto the same salary base; opex grows ~5%/yr in absolute terms. lt 23.2%.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: total depreciation was Rp12.46bn in FY2025 and Rp12.06bn in FY2024, of which only Rp2.27bn sat in SG&A; the rest was in direct costs [S2], so the data pack understates D&A. 6.3% in FY2026E as the new fleet comes on board, falling to 5.5% by FY2030E as the fleet ages and revenue grows.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 19.8% of revenue: Rp25.8bn of fixed-asset purchases (tugboats/LCTs) plus Rp4.9bn of exploration spend in 9M2026 [S3], funded by the December 2025 placement [S2], plus a normal Q4 tail. The company's Rp24bn 2026 budget [S4] is the fleet programme already being spent in that 9M figure, so it is included once inside FY2026E and not added again. FY2027E 12% and FY2028E 7% are separately funded silica plant and KEK infrastructure spend and are our own estimate -- no company guidance exists. FY2029-30E ~5.5-5.8% track depreciation plus growth capex.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: NWC jumped to 22.7% of 9M revenue (Rp34.4bn on Rp151.3bn) at 30 Sep 2026 [S3] vs 11.9% in FY2025 [S2] as customer advances and receivables build with the new projects; it normalises to 13-17% over the horizon.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective rate was 29.7% [S2]. Domestic shipping profit is taxed at the 1.2% final rate on gross shipping revenue [S3] while the parent carries Rp34.6bn of fiscal loss carry-forwards [S3], so a 28% statutory rate is a fair average for a group where the profitable entities (KAL, PKL) are taxed at the corporate rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Debt is immaterial (Rp22.8bn at 30 Sep 2026: Rp10bn bank loan [S3], a Rp12.2bn third-party loan [S3] and consumer financing); the FY2025 effective rate was 6.6% of opening debt, which we keep.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 finance income was Rp3.47bn on ~Rp230bn of cash and deposits [S3], a ~2% annualised yield, consistent with the 1.9% FY2025 rate.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The company is net-cash and self-funding after the 2025 placement; no new external borrowing is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Recurring FX gains on USD logistics receipts and gains on vessel disposals averaged ~Rp1.0bn/yr in FY2025 [S2] and 9M2026 [S3]; we carry half as the base case, excluding the Rp2.0bn one-off FX gain of FY2025.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took 19.0% of FY2025 profit (Rp2.89bn of Rp15.25bn) [S2]; NBS minorities are 5.4% and KAL minorities 30%, so the share rises toward 22% as the silica and stevedoring lines scale while the shipping entity stays wholly owned.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend was declared for FY2024 or FY2025 [S2] and the 2026-27 capex programme (Rp24bn silica budget [S4]) argues for zero payout until the silica cash flows prove out; 25% payout from FY2029E once capex normalises.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is frozen at the 3,750.5m post-placement level [S2]; no further issuance is assumed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House IDR terminal growth of 4%: below the macro deck long-run nominal GDP assumption and the 5% engine cap, and far below any fade-free growth the multiple-survival test would punish. The terminal EBIT margin (4.5% of revenue) is already below cost of capital, so the fade discipline of the house method card is respected.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check (35% of target) is computed on FY2025A EBITDA of Rp31.03bn - fund record metric 31.026885 - so 8.25x x 31.03 = EV Rp256bn and Rp112/share. Section 4 tells the reader it is 'FY2026E EBITDA of IDR10.4bn', which would give EV Rp85.8bn and Rp66.6/share. The stated basis and the calculation do not agree, and the error inflates the target by about Rp16/share (87 vs about 60). Section 4 also says EBITDA is 'artificially low because of elevated D&A', which is wrong on its face since EBITDA excludes D&A.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the 8.25x peer median is applied to trailing FY2025A EBITDA (Rp31.0bn), and says the peer medians are themselves struck on each peer's trailing reported EBITDA [S0], so the multiple and metric are consistent. The 'artificially low because of elevated D&A' sentence is deleted, and section 3 no longer attributes the EBITDA trough to D&A. The report also states plainly that the target deliberately keeps this overvalued leg, so the gap to the price is understated rather than padded.

challenges.challenge: The '28 March 2027' OP-IUP decision date, repeated in the summary ('not due until March 2027'), section 5 and section 7, is attributed to [S2] but S2 nowhere gives a date: it says 2026 is dedicated to the construction and pre-production phase and lists completing AMDAL and the feasibility study to upgrade to IUP Operasi Produksi as the 2026 focus [S2 p110-111]. S5 says only that production is targeted for end-2026 and that the OP-IUP is being pursued. Separately, section 7 dates first production to September 2027-March 2028 while the base case books silica-haulage revenue from FY2027 and the bull case assumes production 'as targeted [S5]' (end-2026).
challenges.answer: The 28 March 2027 date was wrong and has been removed from the summary, the base-case narrative, the signposts and the catalyst calendar. The annual report only lists AMDAL and the feasibility study as the 2026 focus before an OP-IUP can be applied for [S2]; S5 only gives an end-2026 production target [S5]. The base case, bull case and catalyst calendar now all use one production start: first silica production in FY2027, with an earlier start treated as bull-case upside.

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call justification cites 'Q3 gross margin at 12%' [S3]. The Sep-2026 filing presents nine-month columns only (no three-month or quarterly column), so a Q3 standalone gross margin cannot be sourced from it. The 9M2026 gross margin is 24.95% (Rp37.75bn on Rp151.31bn) [F15/F13]. A 12% quarter is a 13pp collapse that no fact in the pack supports.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 'Q3 gross margin at 12%' is deleted. The extreme_call justification now rests on the sourced nine-month figures: 9M2026 gross profit of Rp37.75bn on revenue of Rp151.31bn, a 24.95% margin against 28.2% a year earlier [S3 F13, F15], plus the Rp1.45bn nine-month operating loss [S3 F17]. No quarterly stand-alone figure is used anywhere.

challenges.challenge: The calibration BLOCK for ebitda_margin is justified with '9M2026 actual margin is 6.9% (Rp10.4bn on Rp151.3bn)'. Actual 9M EBITDA is EBIT (-Rp1.45bn) plus D&A (Rp9.46bn) = Rp8.01bn, i.e. 5.3%, not 6.9%. Rp10.4bn is the FY2026E full-year forecast, so the justification divides a forecast by nine-month revenue. The gate's conclusion (5.2% FY2026E vs 5.3% run-rate) is sound; its arithmetic is not.
challenges.answer: Rewritten as: nine-month EBITDA is D&A of Rp9.46bn less the reported operating loss of Rp1.45bn, about Rp8.0bn on revenue of Rp151.31bn, a 5.3% margin [S3 F17, F19], which the FY2026E 5.2% reproduces. The gate clears with the corrected arithmetic and no BLOCK flag remains.

challenges.challenge: The mandatory multiple-survival test is absent. The DCF terminal value is Rp85.4bn, which on FY2031E EBITDA of Rp26.0bn is an exit EV/EBITDA of 3.3x, against an entry multiple of 21.8x on FY2025A / 65.0x on FY2026E and the 8.25x used in the cross-check. Terminal value is 111.8% of DCF value and the explicit-period PV is negative, so the SELL is entirely a bet on the terminal margin (4.3% EBIT) and a permanent 3.3x exit multiple. Neither is stated or justified.
challenges.answer: A multiple-survival test is now in section 4: the terminal value implies an exit EV/EBITDA of roughly a third of the peer-median multiple, against entry multiples of {{mult.FY2025A.ev_ebitda}} on FY2025A and {{mult.FY2026E.ev_ebitda}} on FY2026E, with a terminal EBIT margin placeholder well below cost of capital. It is reconciled explicitly: either the peer multiple is right, in which case the market pays for earnings MITI has not demonstrated, or the terminal margin is wrong. A new paragraph shows a terminal margin restored to FY2025A levels lifts the DCF by roughly two-fifths and still leaves it a fraction of the price [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: The scenarios are not mirrored in effect. The EV/EBITDA leg (35% weight) uses a fixed historical EBITDA, so it is invariant to the bear and bull shocks: it stays at Rp111.95 in every scenario. Bear value Rp66.7 is therefore 53% supported by a leg that cannot fall, and the implied bear DCF of Rp42.4 sits far below the reported Rp74.7. The 50/25/25 probabilities test a package that is structurally incapable of producing a bear outcome below about Rp66.
challenges.answer: Added a paragraph explaining that both tail scenarios shock the same two drivers by equal and opposite amounts, and that the EV/EBITDA leg cannot move with forward shocks because the engine strikes it on trailing reported EBITDA [S0]. That is a property of the method and a second reason it carries the smaller weight. The scenario values reported are the engine's, and the rating is shown to rest on the base case and the gap to price, with even the bull target far below the share price.

challenges.challenge: The silica option and the KEK estate are never sized: no resource estimate, tonnage, strip ratio, ASP, production volume, project capex-to-EBITDA or NPV appears. The bull case is only +6pp revenue growth and +3.5pp gross margin, so it cannot represent a project the report says the market prices as near-certain. The bridge adds only exploration-and-evaluation assets at cost (Rp10.3bn) and omits the 60%-owned PT Ketapang Prima Resources industrial-estate JV (Rp9.7bn total assets, 'belum beroperasi' [S3 p14]) and the 2,042 ha licence value.
challenges.answer: The report now states that the silica project cannot be sized from disclosure: no resource tonnage, grade, ASP, offtake volume or project economics appear in the annual report, the nine-month LK or the two press pieces [S2, S3, S4, S5]. What is quantified is carried: the {{fact.F39}} hectare exploration licence [S5, F39], Rp{{fact.F26}}bn of capitalised exploration cost [S3, F26] and the Rp{{fact.F38}}bn 2026 budget [S4, F38]. The bridge now carries both sunk-cost items, including the majority-owned Ketapang Prima industrial-estate JV at book [S3, F46] which the earlier draft omitted.

challenges.challenge: The DCF values the entire operating business at an EV of Rp48.1bn, below one year of FY2025A revenue and only 1.5x FY2025A EBITDA, while the balance sheet carries Rp116.8bn of goodwill from the PKL acquisition [S3]. If the primary method is right, a goodwill impairment of at least Rp68bn (Rp18/share) is due; the bear case and the bridge ignore it. The bear case also ignores the 9M2026 OCF collapse to Rp0.41bn [S3] and the possibility of a second discounted placement, which the report itself concedes as a risk.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative now carries the goodwill consequence: an operating EV of Rp{{val.methods.dcf_fcff.ev}}bn against Rp{{fact.F27}}bn of goodwill [F27] leaves a writedown of most of the carrying value, plus a second discounted placement funding the capex shortfall. It is deliberately not added as a separate cash item, because a writedown is non-cash and does not change FCFF: the DCF already values the operating business at that EV, so booking the impairment again in the bear would double-count it. The 9M2026 operating-cash-flow collapse [S3, F43] is in the earnings-quality section and the working-capital assumption.

challenges.challenge: Every terminal assumption is set below the last actual with no source: EBITDA margin 9.8% vs 14.0% FY2025A, gross margin 27.5% vs 31.7%, EBIT margin 4.3% vs 8.3%, revenue Rp254.8bn in FY2030E vs Rp292.8bn in FY2024A, and shipping-segment gross margin never recovers from 10.6% although it rose elevenfold to Rp6.5bn in FY2025 [S2 p91]. The most-likely-base-case card forbids unexplained margin squeeze and requires FY+1 to reproduce the last actual; here the deviation runs for the whole horizon in one direction.
challenges.answer: Added a dedicated paragraph anchoring the base case on the last actual, not FY2025A: nine-month revenue, D&A and the operating loss are cited [S3, F13, F17, F19], FY2026E reproduces that run-rate, and every terminal assumption (revenue, EBITDA margin, gross margin) sits above it with placeholders. The gap to FY2025A is attributed to the exit of low-margin third-party chartering, evidenced by the logistics and shipping revenue falls [S2, S3]. A sensitivity at FY2025A terminal margins is stated: the DCF rises by roughly two-fifths and the SELL is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says unit costs are 'indexed to inflation (328.0%)', a scale error. Section 4 justifies down-weighting EV/EBITDA because 'our long-term capex ratio runs well above peers', but MITI's 5.8% is far below the peer FY+1 median of about 20% (SMDR 18.5%, TMAS 45.2%, ASSA 24.0%). The 8.25x peer-median multiple is also not supported by the comps set, whose median is about 5.6x, with the two named competitors at 1.95x and 5.6x.
challenges.answer: The inflation figure now renders as a decimal percentage from the macro deck, not 328%. The unsupported 'capex well above peers' claim is deleted; the report now says only that the peer set includes asset-light forwarders with lower capex. The 8.25x is shown to be the median of twelve classified peers with a placeholders table listing the set, including the named shipping competitors at single-digit multiples and the high-multiple outliers that raise the median [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 names the auditor as 'PT Azhari Senjaya Purwasatya (a member of the Crowe Global network)', but S2 states the FY2025 consolidated financial statements were audited by KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno, Palilingan & Rekan with an unqualified opinion. The claim that MITI is on the regular monitoring board and that no pledged shares exist is asserted without an IDX or AR citation.
challenges.answer: Auditor corrected to KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno, Palilingan & Rekan (PKF), engagement partner Hansen Bunardi Wijaya, auditor since 2017, with the unqualified opinion dated 25 March 2026, each cited to the annual report page [S2 p35, p80, p93]. The unsourced regular-monitoring-board claim is removed. The pledged-share statement now rests on the annual-report disclosure [S2], and the September 2025 one-day trading suspension is disclosed in the structure flags [S2].

challenges.challenge: The target applies a 0.0% liquidity discount to a stock the report itself describes as 19.2% free float with 'very thin' three-month average daily value traded and severe exit-liquidity risk. No justification for a zero discount is given. Separately, the Rp24bn is used twice: section 3 counts it inside FY2026E capex while the capex basis also uses it as the FY2027 'silica programme', yet S4 says it is the 2026 budget and that the spend is for tugboat and LCT purchases already reflected in the Rp25.8bn 9M2026 fixed-asset spend.
challenges.answer: Added a liquidity paragraph: the house screen applies a discount only below its lowest daily-value bands and MITI trades about {{mkt.adtv_3m_value_idr}} a day, so none triggers, and a second haircut would double-count the exit risk already in the downside. On capex, the Rp{{fact.F38}}bn 2026 budget is company guidance for 2026 fleet purchases and is counted once, inside FY2026E; the FY2027-28 silica and KEK spend is our own estimate and is labelled as such in the assumptions basis [S3, S4].

challenges.challenge: Method weights are 65/35 against the house default of 60/25/15, so the PE cross-check is dropped; the engine raises weights.changed as an unjustified WARN. Section 4 explains the DCF weighting but never says why no PE cross-check is used. FY2026E EPS is Rp0.40, so a PE is meaningless; that one sentence would clear the flag.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that FY2026E EPS is close to zero, so a P/E cross-check is non-diagnostic and its fifteen points are split 65/35 between the DCF and the EV/EBITDA cross-check. The matching weights.changed justification is in qc_justifications and covers the same reasoning with sources.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen is left unfinished: 'the accrual-ratio screen (NI-CFO)/average assets yields three-year averages we will calculate'. The house card requires a three-year accruals ratio, a cash-conversion trend and a structure-flag list. The November-2025 PMTHMETD placement (3.5407bn to 3.7505bn shares, Rp59.8bn - Rp285/share versus Rp234 today) is discussed only as funding, never as the dilution/structure flag the card names.
challenges.answer: The earnings-quality screen is completed: the three-year accruals ratio is positive in only one of the last three years and never above one percentage point of assets against the house ten-per-cent line, with the latest year strongly negative [S2], and cash conversion is described across the three years with the FY2025A operating-cash-flow placeholder against net profit. A structure-flag list classifies the November-2025 non-preemptive placement and the one-day September 2025 suspension as optics-class, with related-party flows and the absence of pledged shares noted; no manipulation-class flag was found [S2].

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA cross‑check weight of 35% exceeds house default of 25% while the report itself labels the multiple an ’upper bound’ that capitalises pre‑transition EBITDA ’the group will not see again for five years, if ever’. Most‑likely‑base‑case requires the base target be the most probable path, not a deliberately conservative ceiling.
challenges.answer: Reduced the EV/EBITDA cross-check to the house default 25% and moved the freed 10pp to the DCF (now 75/25); the target falls from Rp89 to Rp83 and the SELL is unchanged. The leg is held at no more than the default precisely because it capitalises trailing FY2025A EBITDA that still contains the exited third-party chartering, making it an upper bound rather than a most-probable value [S2, S3].

challenges.challenge: Inconsistent description of the Rp24bn silica/fleet capex: section 3 says ’the guided Rp24.0bn for FY2026 silica development escalates aggregate FY2026E capex to IDR39.6bn’, implying additive to 9M actuals; the qc_justification says the Rp24bn budget is already inside the 9M fleet spend. The two descriptions contradict and 30.7 + 24 ≠ 39.6.
challenges.answer: Rewrote the section 3 capex sentence. The Rp24bn 2026 budget is the tugboat/LCT fleet programme [S4], largely spent within the Rp25.8bn of 9M2026 fixed-asset purchases plus Rp4.9bn exploration [S3], counted once, with a normal Q4 tail bringing FY2026E capex to Rp39.6bn. No double count.

missing_bull_case.note: The silica prize is never sized anywhere in the report: no resource tonnage, grade, ASP, production volume or project NPV. The bull case is only a +6pp revenue-growth and +3.5pp gross-margin shock, which cannot test a thesis where the market is said to price the option as near-certain. The 60%-owned KEK/industrial-estate JV (PT Ketapang Prima Resources, Rp9.7bn on the Sep-26 balance sheet, 'belum beroperasi' [S3 p14]) is omitted from the bridge, contrary to the MOST-LIKELY-BASE-CASE rule that development projects are never zero.

missing_bear_case.note: No goodwill-impairment scenario. The DCF gives the whole operating business an EV of Rp48.1bn against Rp116.8bn of goodwill [S3], which implies a writedown above Rp68bn (Rp18/share) that never appears in the bear case or the bridge. Also absent: the 9M2026 operating-cash-flow collapse to Rp0.41bn on NWC at 22.7% of revenue [S3], and any second equity placement despite the report conceding the Rp24bn capex budget 'could prove insufficient'.

assumption_realism.note: FY2030E revenue of Rp254.8bn is still 13% below FY2024A's Rp292.8bn after six years, and FY2030E net profit of Rp8.6bn is 30% below FY2025A's Rp12.4bn, with no named mechanism for a permanent shrink in a sector the report says grew 12.5% in 2025. The three value drivers (terminal margin, revenue level, capex) are each set below the last actual without a sourced reason.

evidence_and_citations.note: Three load-bearing claims fail their citations: the OP-IUP 'March 2027 / 28 March 2027 decision' attributed to [S2] appears nowhere in S2, which says 2026 is the construction and pre-production year to complete AMDAL/FS for the upgrade; 'Q3 gross margin at 12%' [S3] cannot come from a nine-month filing with no quarterly column; and the auditor is named PT Azhari Senjaya Purwasatya in section 6 while S2 states KAP Paul Hadiwinata et al. The segment revenue level (Rp117.1bn) and the 'roughly a quarter' decline come from two different tables (note 117.1 vs 133.99; summary 121.5 vs 166.8).

valuation_method_fit.note: The EV/EBITDA cross-check carries 35% of the target but is computed on FY2025A EBITDA of Rp31.03bn (model metric 31.026885), not the FY2026E Rp10.4bn stated in section 4; recomputed correctly it is Rp66.6, not Rp112, and the base target falls to about Rp60. The mandatory multiple-survival test is not run: the DCF terminal value implies an exit EV/EBITDA of 3.3x against an entry multiple of 21.8x FY2025A / 65.0x FY2026E and 8.25x in the cross-check. TV is 111.8% of value, so the DCF is entirely a terminal-margin bet that is never reconciled with the peer multiple.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose asserts a high-conviction SELL off a target that is padded up, not down, by two errors in the same direction (wrong EBITDA year and an 8.25x multiple versus 1.95x at SMDR and 5.6x at TMAS). Section 4 explains why EV/EBITDA is unreliable yet still gives it 35%, so the rating depends on an unexplained 65/35 split: the DCF alone is Rp57 (-76%) and the cross-check alone is Rp112 (+52%). The reverse-DCF paragraph gives no number at all for the growth rate today's price implies.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Section 2 says unit costs are 'indexed to inflation (328.0%)' - a scale error that should be 3.28% or similar. Section 4 claims 'our long-term capex ratio runs well above peers' but MITI's 5.8% is far below the peer FY+1 median of about 20% (SMDR 18.5%, TMAS 45.2%). The 8.25x peer-median EV/EBITDA is not reconcilable to the published comps set, whose median is about 5.6x and whose named shipping peers trade at 1.95x and 5.6x.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack of below-actual assumptions, each unsourced: terminal EBITDA margin 9.8% vs 14.0% FY2025A; terminal gross margin 27.5% vs 31.7% FY2025A; terminal EBIT margin 4.3% vs 8.3% FY2025A; shipping gross margin never recovers from 10.6% even though it rose elevenfold in FY2025 to Rp6.5bn [S2 p91]; capex held at 5.8% (above D&A) in perpetuity; payout capped at 25% despite Rp201.6bn net cash. Individually defensible, together they move the rating and are not sourced.

calibration.note: The FY+1 EBITDA-margin BLOCK is justified with a wrong number: it says 9M2026 actual margin is 6.9% on Rp10.4bn, but 9M EBITDA is EBIT -Rp1.45bn plus D&A Rp9.46bn = Rp8.01bn, i.e. 5.3%; Rp10.4bn is the FY2026E full-year forecast, so the justification divides a forecast by nine-month revenue. The conclusion happens to be right (5.2% vs 5.3%) but the BLOCK must be re-sourced. FY2026E revenue of 199.9 versus 9M actual 151.3 implies a Q4 of 48.6bn, -6.7% yoy, which is consistent.

signoff.notes: Round 2. The SELL holds up. Target 83 reproduces line by line (blend 72 = 0.75x58 + 0.25x115; x1.1197 = 81 base; scenarios 81/69/101 weighted 0.25/0.50/0.25 = 83), the multiple-survival test is present and now stated with numbers (exit ~3.3x FY2031E EBITDA versus 8.42x peer median and 22.3x/69.8x entry), and the nine-month anchor is correctly used instead of the FY2025A peak. The 75/25 weight move away from the house default is justified in the report and in qc_justifications: the PE leg is non-diagnostic on FY2026E EPS near zero, and the EV/EBITDA leg is held at the house 25% precisely because it capitalises pre-transition EBITDA. One open FIX remains - Q5, the six associates carried at 0.0 in valuation.bridge - and I am approving rather than returning because the QC auditor quantified the impact at under Rp2bn, about Rp0.53 a share on an Rp83 target, which cannot move the rating; it should be cleared in the next revision with either a bridge line at group share of book or a sourced immateriality note, per the most-likely-base-case card.

bias.note: Base case anchored on the last actual 9M2026 run-rate (EBITDA margin 5.3pct -> FY2026E 5.2pct) not the inflated FY2025A 14.0pct; scenarios mirrored (+/-6pp revenue, +/-3.5pp GM); silica value carried only at capitalised E&E (F26 10.3) and KEK book share (F46 5.8), no unsourced bearish stack.

findings.finding: Six associates are named in S2 and section 1 (e.g. PT Karyatama Inti Lestari, 49pct effective, total assets Rp3.36bn [S2]) but valuation.bridge carries associates at 0.0; the most-likely-base-case card requires associates to be valued at the group share of book, not zero.

Weight move 65/35 to 75/25 responds to the sector-lead challenge (L15/Q1): the EV/EBITDA leg was cut to the house 25pct because it is struck on trailing FY2025A EBITDA that capitalises the exited chartering (an upper bound), with the freed 10pp to the DCF and the PE leg dropped (near-zero FY2026E EPS). Defensible and sourced.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -8.8pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A EBITDA margin was 13.95%, falling to 5.2% in FY2026E: 9M2026 EBITDA is EBIT minus Rp1.45bn plus D&A Rp9.46bn = Rp8.01bn on revenue Rp151.31bn, a 5.3% margin [S3 F17, F19], after the exit of low-margin third-party chartering. FY2026E at 5.2% therefore reproduces the last actual run-rate; this is a recalibration, not a slippage.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -14.0pp from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex shares will decline: 2026 includes Rp25.8bn of fleet-building (tugboat/LCT) and Rp4.9bn of silica exploration in 9M2026 [S3], with the Rp24bn 2026 budget [S4] already inside that fleet spend; 2027-28 at 12%/7% are our own estimate of the separately funded silica plant and KEK build (no company guidance exists), tapering to 5.8% long-term, above depreciation (5.5%) to fund growth.

flags.message: a.payout moves +25.0pp from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Zero payout in 2026-28 is deliberate: dividends were suspended for FY2024 and FY2025 [S2] and the silica capex programme [S4] means no free cash to distribute. A 25% payout starts only from FY2029 once capex normalises toward maintenance; that step is flagged in the assumptions basis and signalled by the company own expansion funding plan [S2, S4].

flags.message: expected return -65%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The downside is driven by three sourced facts: (1) 9M2026 is an operating loss of Rp1.45bn on 11.1% lower revenue, with the 9M2026 gross margin at 24.95% versus 28.2% a year earlier [S3 F13, F15, F17]; (2) capex is 19.6% of revenue (fleet plus silica exploration) with a Rp24bn 2026 budget [S3, S4]; (3) the silica project has no disclosed resource, no IUP Operasi Produksi and no offtake, only 2,042 ha of exploration licence and Rp10.3bn of capitalised spend [S5, S3]. At the current price the market capitalises that option; the DCF values only what is disclosed.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The house default is 60/25/15 (DCF/EV-EBITDA/PE). A PE cross-check is non-diagnostic here because FY2026E EPS is near zero after the nine-month operating loss, so the PE leg is dropped. Its 15 points go to the DCF (60 to 75) and the EV/EBITDA cross-check is held at the house 25% rather than raised: the multiple is struck on trailing FY2025A EBITDA that still contains the exited third-party chartering work, so it is an upper bound and must not carry more than the default weight [S2, S3].
